description: Implement static scope as a chain of Environment frames with define, lookup, and assign, and see how shadowing and block exit work.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Each `Environment` frame holds a dictionary `self.vars`, a `self.parent` pointer to the enclosing scope (or `None` at the global root), and `self.name`. `define(name, value)` writes directly into `self.vars[name]` without inspecting `self.parent`.

`lookup(name)` starts at `env = self` and loops while `env is not None`. If `name in env.vars`, it returns `env.vars[name]` immediately (line 21); otherwise it follows `env = env.parent` one hop outward (line 24). It raises `NameError` if it runs off the end.

`assign(name, value)` walks the same `env.parent` chain to overwrite the nearest existing binding of `name`, raising `NameError` if no frame defines it. `__repr__` formats the chain from inner frame to outer frame separated by `' -> '`.

Compare `define` (line 10) with `assign` (lines 30-35): `define` always creates or overwrites a binding in `self.vars`, whereas `assign` searches outward and updates whichever enclosing frame already holds `name`.

Lines 45-47 define `a = 1` and `b = 2` in `glob`. Line 49 creates child frame `block = Environment(parent=glob, name="block")`, defines `b = 20` and `c = 30` inside `block`, and evaluates `P1` inside `block`. It then switches back to `glob` at `P2`.

steps.answer: `block.lookup("a")` misses in `block` and finds `1` in `glob`, while `block.lookup("b")` (`20`) and `block.lookup("c")` (`30`) stop immediately in `block`, printing `P1: 51`.
steps.question: On line 52, `block.lookup("a") + block.lookup("b") + block.lookup("c")` runs inside `block`. Which frame supplies each of `'a'`, `'b'`, and `'c'`, and what sum is printed for `P1`?

steps.description: During `block.lookup("a")`, `'a'` is not in `block.vars`, so line 24 advances `env = env.parent` to `glob`, where `'a'` resolves to `1`.

title: Walking a Chain of Environment Frames
